rationale: Workload-class weights for the throughput denominator S_B = exp(sum_i w_i * ln(r_i)), where r_i = throughput_franken_i / throughput_baseline_i over equivalence-passing workloads. Weights are assigned per workload CLASS (not per hand-picked workload) to reflect the relative prevalence of each class in representative real-world Node/Bun server-side and tooling workloads. Within a class, the class weight is split equally across the member workloads that are actually admitted (equivalence-passing) into the run, and class weights are renormalised over the classes that have at least one admitted member so that the per-case weights always sum to 1.0. This makes the score robust to a class being entirely quarantined for a given baseline while keeping the cross-class weighting fixed by policy rather than by per-run cherry-picking.

weight_policy.normalization: class weights renormalised over admitted classes; per-class weight split equally across admitted members

workload_classes.description: JSON parse/stringify on small, medium, and deeply nested payloads — dominant in API servers and config tooling.
Request routing, header parsing, and response serialization — the dominant server-side hot path for both Node and Bun.
String concatenation, template assembly, encode/decode, and regex matching common to templating and validation layers.
Hashing, HMAC, and symmetric crypto used in auth, signing, and content-addressing paths.
Numeric and algorithmic compute (recurrences, sorting, matrix ops) representing data-transform and scientific workloads.
Module resolution, ESM/CJS interop, and cold-start initialization — heavily weighted in CLI and serverless tooling.
